text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny accused the opposition of delaying the pension reform.
- The government says Parliament absolutely must pass 30 bills and draft resolutions before the summer recess.
- Hungarian state television expects to suffer losses of two billion forints this year and its balance sheet will show further losses of six billion forints.
- Young Democrat president Viktor Orban denied Monday an assumption that the governing coalition is to be blamed for the disruption of the opposition.
- The last draftee border guards will be demobilized next April, and from then on only professionals will be on duty.
- Interest groups of small and middle-sized businesses met Monday to object against the government's economic policy, which they say is disadvantageous to them.
- Socialist MP Lajos Varga gave up his parliamentary seat as he has an executive posotion at a state-owned company, thus he is affected by the conflict of interest law.
- President Arpad Goncz yesterday unveiled a memorial column in memory of one-time premier Imre Nagy at Snagov, Romania.
Russia is offering MIG and Suhoy fighter jets to Hungary at competitive prices, a visiting Russian official said.
- Domestic foreign currency savings dropped 4.6 billion forints in April to 477.1 billion forints.
- The BUX Index hit a new record on Monday, when it rose 117.7 points to close at 5,991.32.
- Gyula Lengyel, managing director of the Hungarian Electricity Works (MVM) resigned at the Monday AGM.
-Telecoms Matav Rt closed last year with a balance sheet profit of 23.6 billion forints, on sales of 196.5 billion forints, 37% up on 1995, the AGM was informed yesterday.
- Privatization agency APV Rt posted revenues of 75 billion forints so far this year, in line with the 180 billion forints full-year target.
- Hungaria Biztosito Rt. closed last year with a balance sheet profit of 4.4 billion forints, up 18.5% on a year earlier, on premium revenues of 49.9 billion forints, a 21% increase.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Gas distributor Ddgaz Rt. closed 1996 with a loss of Ft 542 million forints on net sales of more than 10 billion forints, president and CEO Otto Gaal said.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Power plant Matrai Eromu Rt, owned by the German consortium of RWE Energie AG and EVS AG, closed last year with profits of 504 million forints.
- Some 100 tourists had extended stays in Corfu and Spain when executives of the Taltos Mustang travel agency fled the country without forwarding the payment for their return tickets.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- A senior police official told Vilaggazdasag Monday that the Russian and other European and Asian organized crime gangs operating in Budapest have cemented their positions in catering and prostitution, but have failed to achieve significant results in trade and the gambling industry.
